node-1.label: A woman in her 40s presented with a 3-year history of a complex progressive disorder characterized by emotional lability, cognitive decline, generalized ataxia, and autonomic dysfunction

node-2.label: Autonomic testing revealed abnormal cardiac parasympathetic function without orthostatic hypotension, patchy decrease in sweat output on quantitative sudomotor axon reflex test, and markedly abnormal thermoregulatory sweat test with near complete global anhidrosis

node-3.label: Patient denied paresthesias, dysesthesias, or loss of sensation

why.why: Radiology, laboratory, and pathology expert analyses uniformly interpret the bilateral pulvinar hyperintensity, diffuse volume loss, elevated CSF protein without pleocytosis, and autonomic dysfunction with anhidrosis as supporting a CNS neurodegenerative process. The absence of sensory symptoms favors central autonomic involvement, and the positive pseudo-α-galactosidase allele is considered incidental. Confidence increased from 0.78 to 0.85, though definitive confirmation still requires pending RT-QuIC, EEG, PRNP, and genetic/autoimmune testing.

Expert analyses emphasize that the CSF is non-inflammatory (elevated protein without pleocytosis) and the MRI pattern is neurodegenerative rather than inflammatory; the positive pseudo-α-galactosidase allele is incidental and does not support an immune-mediated process. These findings further reduce the likelihood of immune-mediated ataxia. Confidence decreased from 0.10 to 0.05.

Expert analyses agree that the absence of sensory symptoms and the central pattern of autonomic dysfunction (near-global anhidrosis with parasympathetic failure) favor a central autonomic process rather than peripheral autonomic neuropathy. The MRI and CSF findings also point to CNS neurodegeneration. Confidence decreased from 0.04 to 0.02.

MRI shows structural neurodegeneration (bilateral pulvinar hyperintensity and diffuse volume loss) and CSF shows elevated protein without pleocytosis, which are not features of toxic/metabolic encephalopathy. No toxic exposure or metabolic derangement has been identified; confidence decreased from 0.05 to 0.02.
